children: The Sub Contract Works (including the selection of the kind and standard of materials, goods and workmanship and including any variations instructed in accordance with this Sub Contract) will when designed, constructed and completed comply with any performance specifications, standard or requirement included or referred to in the Contract Documents.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor shall start the Sub Contract Works on the Commencement Date. The Contract Sum is inclusive of all costs necessary to complete the Sub Contract Works and includes but is not limited to all costs associated with revisions to the planned programme including out of sequence working, restrictions on working hours, methods of working, vehicular site access including parking and any other restraints affecting the timing and method of construction.

children.name: text
children: Any programme provided by the Company to the Sub Contractor is indicative only and is subject to amendment as the Project progresses. The Sub Contractor is responsible for providing adequate resources to keep in line with actual progress of the current programme.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor is responsible for providing all relevant information to the Company to allow for planning of the programme.

children.name: text
children: If the Commencement Date is to be later than specified in the Sub Contract Agreement the Company will inform the Sub Contractor of the revised commencement date (which will be confirmed by the Company in writing) and adjust the programme for the Sub Contract Works accordingly.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor shall proceed with the Sub Contract Works in accordance with the progress of the Main Contract Works.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contract Works shall be carried out and completed in accordance with the programme details stated in the Sub Contract Agreement and reasonably in accordance with the progress of the Main Contract Works or each relevant Section of them, [subject, as respects construction but not design work, to receipt by the Sub Contractor of notice to commence work in accordance with the Sub Contract Agreement].

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contract Works on Site shall be undertaken during normal working hours as specified in the Sub Contract Agreement.

children.name: text
children: If the Sub Contractor is failing to proceed regularly and diligently with the Sub Contract Works, the Company may direct the Sub Contractor to bring to Site alternative and/or additional resources and the Sub Contractor shall forthwith comply with this direction entirely at his own cost.

children.name: text
children: If the Sub Contractor fails to proceed with due diligence or through his own fault is in delay or fails to complete the Sub Contract Works in accordance with the Sub Contract or by his acts or omissions adversely affects the regular progress of the Sub Contract Works or Main Contract Works the Sub Contractor shall indemnify the Company a sum equivalent to any loss and/or expense incurred by the Company or likely to be suffered or incurred by the Company by reason of the default, failure or acts or omissions of the Sub Contractor. Such sums shall include but not limited to, such loss and/or expense as the Company may be liable to pay under the Main Contract Works or such other sum as the Company may from time to time reasonably estimate as the amount of such loss and/or expense that maybe incurred and or be liable to pay under the Main Contract or any other Sub Contract or other third party agreement entered into in connection with the Main Contract. The Company shall be entitled to deduct any sum payable under this sub-clause from any amounts which may at any time be due or have become due to the Sub Contractor from the Company under the Sub Contract or otherwise.

children.name: text
children: If pursuant to clause 13.3 the Company grants an extension of time for completion of the Sub Contract Works and/or of any part then the Company shall pay or repay the Sub Contractor any amounts recovered, allowed or paid under clause 11.9 for the periods of such extension.

children.name: text
children: The total amount of loss and/or expense in respect only of delay to the completion of the Sub Contract Works and/or any part shall be limited to the appropriate sum stated in the Sub Contract Particulars. If no such limit is stated therein then such loss and/or expense without limit shall apply.

children.name: text
children: The Company will at the request of the Sub Contractor advise the Sub Contractor in writing of the date of practical completion and the date of the expiry of the Defects Liability Period. The Sub Contract Works will not be practically complete unless and until the Sub Contractor has supplied any as-built drawings, warranties, guarantees, test documentation, manuals and any other documents required under this Agreement.

children.name: text
children: The Company shall notify the Sub Contractor of any defects that appear in the Sub Contract Works during the Defects Liability Period. The Sub Contractor shall at its own cost make good such defects within the timescales as stated in the Company’s notification or where none is stated as soon as reasonably practicable.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor shall make good any defects, shrinkages, omissions and other faults notified or instructed under clause 12.2 in such a way as to enable the Company to comply with the Main Contract Works and in any event in such a way as to cause the least delay, damage, inconvenience or disruption to the Company, the Owner, any Purchaser and/or Tenant occupying the Property (or any part thereof) and their respective business or activities or any fitting-out works and the Sub Contractor shall comply with any reasonable directions and security precautions of any occupier of the Property.

children.name: text
children: In the event that the Sub Contractor fails to respond to the notification within a reasonable time or at all or if the Sub Contractor otherwise fails to remedy any defect then the Company may employ and pay others to carry out the work and recover any additional cost from the Sub Contractor as a debt.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor shall constantly use its best endeavours to prevent or minimise any delay in the progress of the whole or any part of the Sub Contract Works. The Sub Contractor shall keep the Company informed of the progress of the Sub Contract Works.

children.name: text
children: If at any time it becomes reasonably apparent that the commencement, progress or completion of the Sub Contract Works or part thereof is delayed or likely to be delayed for reasons beyond the control of the Sub Contractor, the Sub Contractor shall forthwith give written notice of the material circumstances including the cause or causes of the delay to the Company and shall identify in the notice any event which in his opinion entitles them to an extension of time under these Conditions.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor shall in such notice or otherwise in writing within a maximum period of 7 days after issue of such notice provide all substantiation of any claim which the Sub Contractor may wish to make for an extension of time given particulars of expected effects of such delay and estimating the extent of any of the expected delay on completion of the Sub Contract Works or part thereof.

children.name: text
children: If upon written application by the Sub Contractor in accordance with clause 13.2 the Company is of the opinion that the regular progress of the Sub Contract Works is likely to be or has been delayed beyond the Period for Completion and that such delay was or will be caused by reasons beyond the Sub Contractor’s control, then the Company shall, (save where these Conditions provide otherwise and having regard to the sufficiency of the Sub Contractor’s notice, particulars and estimates) make in writing a fair and reasonable extension of the Period for Completion. No further or other extension shall be granted in respect of the particular events to which that extension is granted by the Company.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor shall not be entitled (notwithstanding any other provision of these Conditions) to an extension of time where and to the extent the event causing the delay results from any act, error, omission, negligence, default or breach of contract or breach of statutory duty on the part of the Sub Contractor or persons employed by the Sub Contractor.

children.name: text
children: If the Company shall grant an extension of time under clause 13.3 the Sub Contractor shall submit to the Company for approval a revised programme within 14 days of the date on which the Company notifies the Sub Contractor of such extension or issues such instruction.

children.name: text
children: The Company gives no guarantee of continuity of work and may at any time issue an instruction to the Sub Contractor to reduce or extend the Period(s) for Completion and the Sub Contractor shall immediately take such measures as are necessary to comply with such instruction without adjustment to the Contract Sum or any claim for loss and/or expense whatsoever.

children.name: text
children: It shall be a condition precedent to any entitlement to payment that the Sub Contractor shall:

children.name: text
children: take out and maintain any and all insurance cover required under this Sub Contract;

children.name: text
children: provide the collateral warranties, guarantees and bonds required under the Sub Contract which will be in the same form as those required under the Main Contract;

children.name: text
children: provide to the Company all documents necessary to comply with CIS requirements; and

children.name: text
children: execute the Sub Contract as a Deed and return it duly completed to the Company.

Payment of any monies to the Sub Contractor prior to compliance with this condition precedent shall not in any circumstances constitute a waiver of the Company’s right to withhold further payment until the condition precedent has been satisfied.

children.name: text
children: The quality and quantity of the work included in the Contract Sum is that set out in the Contract Documents. The Contract Sum is a fixed price lump sum and shall not be adjusted in any way whatsoever except as provided for in this Sub Contract. (This clause shall apply if identified within the Sub-Contract Agreement)

children.name: text
children: The quality and quantity of the works included in the Contract Sum is that set out in the Contract Documents. The Sub Contract Works shall be subject to a complete re-measurement and the Contract Sum shall be a valuation of all the work executed by the Sub Contractor in accordance with the Sub Contract. The rates and prices set out in the Contract Documents shall be the basis for determining the valuation, and if the Sub Contract Works executed are not of a similar nature in quantity or quality from the works set out in the Contract Documents the work will be valued at fair rates and prices. (This clause shall apply if identified within the Sub-Contract Agreement)

children.name: text
children: The Company shall make interim payments to the Sub Contractor for the Valuation Dates identified in the Sub Contract Particulars and in accordance with the following procedure:

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor shall apply for payment no later than the valuation date specified in the Sub Contract Particulars by submitting to the Company stating the sum it considers due at the due date and the basis on which that sum is calculated. If no Valuation Date is identified in the Sub Contract particulars then the first Valuation Date shall be the last Friday of the month commencing from the start of the Sub Contract Works on site and the last Friday in each subsequent calendar month. Where the Sub Contract Particulars specify fortnightly payments the Valuation Date shall be the second and last Friday in each calendar month. The due date shall be 7 days after the relevant valuation date.

children.name: text
children: No later than 5 days after the due date, the Company shall ascertain the value of the Sub Contract Works properly executed and completed at the due date and shall specify the sum he considers to be or have been due at the due date and the basis on which that sum has been calculated (“Payment Notice” or for final payment “Final Payment Notice”).

children.name: text
children: Subject to any Pay Less Notice, the amount to be paid shall be the amount specified in the Payment Notice or Final Payment Notice.

children.name: text
children: If the Company fails to serve a Payment Notice and the Sub Contractor has applied for payment in accordance with clause 14.3.1 the claim for payment by the Subcontractor, the Company shall pay the amount applied for in the Sub Contractors application for payment subject to any Pay Less Notice (“Default Payment Notice”).

children.name: text
children: If the Company fails to give a Payment Notice in accordance with 14.3.2 and the Sub Contractor has not submitted a claim for payment in accordance with clause 14.3.1 the Sub Contractor may at any time issue a payment notice in default stating the amount it considers to be due and basis upon which that sum is calculated (“Payment Notice in Default”) and the sum to be paid by the Company shall, subject to any notice served under clause 14.3.6 be the sum specified in the Payment Notice in Default. The amount in the Payment Notice or Default Payment Notice or the Payment Notice in Default shall be the “notified sum”. Where either clause 14.3.4 or 14.3.5 apply, the final date for payment shall for all purposes be regarded as postponed by the same number of days as the number of days after expiry of the 5 day period referred to in clause 14.3.2 that the application for payment is made.

children.name: text
children: In the event the Company intends to pay less than the notified sum, the Company shall notify the Sub Contractor of the Companies intention to pay less than the notified sum not later than 5 days before the final date for payment by stating the amount considered to be due at the date the notice is given and the basis on which that sum is calculated (“Pay Less Notice”).

children.name: text
children: No payment will be made for any materials off-site or delivered to site but not yet incorporated into the Sub Contract Works.

children.name: text
children: The final date for any payment shall be:

children.name: text
children: where the Sub Contract Particulars specify fortnightly payments, 14 days after the due date save as for the Final Payment Notice for which the final date for payment shall be 28 days after the due date;

children.name: text
children: where the Sub Contract Particulars specify monthly payments, 35 days after the due date save as for the Final Payment Notice for which the final date for payment shall be 49 days after the due date; and

children.name: text
children: in circumstances where a Payment Notice in Default is served pursuant to clause 14.3.5 the final date for payment shall be extended by a period equal to the period beginning on the date when the Payment Notice should have been served pursuant to clause 14.3.2 and ending on the date when the payment Notice in Default is served.

children.name: text
children: The final date for any payment (unless extended in accordance with clause 14.3.5) shall be 14 days after the due date save as for the Final Payment Notice for which the final date for payment shall be 28 days after the due date. In circumstances where a Payment Notice in Default is served pursuant to clause 14.3.5 the final date for payment shall be extended by a period equal to the period beginning on the date when the Payment Notice should have been served pursuant to clause 14.3.2 and ending on the date when the payment Notice in Default is served.

children.name: text
children: The Company shall be entitled to set-off against any sums otherwise due to the Sub Contractor (arising out of this Sub Contract or under any other trade contract between the Company or a group company and the Sub Contractor) the amount of any damage, cost, losses and expenses which have been incurred by the Company or its associated company for which the Sub Contractor is responsible.

children.name: text
children: The Company is not obliged to pay upon application any sum due if prior to the Company payment, the Main Contractor or any person from whom the Main Contractor is dependent for payment becomes insolvent with the effect that the Company has not been or will not be paid in respect of the Sub Contract Works to which the application relates.

children.name: text
children: The Company shall include with the payment to the Sub Contractor the value added tax properly due provided that the Sub Contractor shall have presented to the Company a valid value added tax invoice. Where the reverse charge output tax applies, the Subcontractor is to account to HMRC for the reverse charge output tax on the VAT exclusive price of items marked 'reverse charge' at the relevant VAT rate.

children.name: text
children: The Final Payment Notice shall be the calculated in accordance with clause 14.3 less any interim payments and show the balance due from the Contractor to the Sub-Contractor or vice versa.

children.name: text
children: All invoices or applications for payment should be received by The Company in accordance with the agreed periods detailed within the Sub Contract Particulars. Notwithstanding, the Company retains the right to reject in full any invoices or applications for payment not received within 45 days of the end of the calendar month in which they were executed.

children.name: text
children: The retention which may be deducted and retained by the Company shall be the percentage stated in the Sub Contract Particulars.

children.name: text
children: The first half of the Sub Contract retention held will become due for release 28 days after the date for practical completion under the Main Contract and the balance shall become due for release 28 days after the date of the defects liability period under the Main Contract, provided always that any defects in the Sub Contract Works have been made good to the Companies satisfaction.

children.name: text
children: Subject to the completion of the Sub-Contract Works in accordance with the Sub-Contract Agreement, the balance of any remaining retention shall become due on completion of the period for making good of defects. Unless stated otherwise within the Sub-contract agreement the Defects Liability or Maintenance Period shall be the period defined within the Main Contract Documents. Provided that if at that time there remains to be executed by the Sub-Contractor any outstanding works, the Contractor may withhold payment until completion of such work.

children.name: text
children: Within 2 weeks of practical completion of the Sub Contract Works the Sub Contractor shall submit to the Company for agreement its detailed final account for the Sub Contract Works carried out.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor’s final account shall be agreed by the Company within 3 months from receipt of all detailed substantiation. In the event that the Sub Contractor fails to submit his final account within stated time period the Company shall ascertain the final Contract Sum which shall then become binding.

children.name: text
children: The Company may terminate the Sub-Contractor’s employment under this Agreement forthwith by written notice if the Sub-Contractor:

children.name: text
children: makes a proposal or enters into an arrangement, compromise or composition in satisfaction of his debts (excluding for the purposes of amalgamation or reconstruction as a solvent company); and/or

children.name: text
children: passes a resolution or makes a determination for voluntary winding-up (except for the purposes of amalgamation or reconstruction); and/or

children.name: text
children: has a winding-up order or bankruptcy order made against him; and/or

children.name: text
children: has a liquidator, administrator or an administrative receiver appointed to him; and/or

children.name: text
children: in the case of a partnership, a partner is the subject of an individual arrangement or proceeding mentioned above; and/or

children.name: text
children: any of the Sub-Contractor’s property is possessed by or on behalf of any holders of any debentures secured by charges over the Project or any part thereof; and/or

children.name: text
children: is the subject of any analogous arrangement, event or proceeding in any other jurisdiction;

children.name: text
children: Any such notice to terminate shall effectively terminate the Contract as at the date of the posting of the notice.

children.name: text
children: In the event that the Sub-Contractor fails to perform regularly and diligently any of its obligations under the Agreement or fails to fully comply with any instruction of the Company, the Company may give written notice to the Sub-Contractor specifying the breach and if the Sub-Contractor fails to remedy the breach within seven days of the date of such notice then the Company may thereafter at such time as it thinks fit terminate the Agreement by giving written notice that the Agreement has been determined with immediate effect.

children.name: text
children: The Company shall be entitled to terminate the Agreement for any reason whatsoever and in circumstances where there is no fault on the part of the Sub-Contractor. The Company shall be entitled to terminate this Agreement at will by seven days written notice of such termination. In the event of such termination, the Sub-Contractor shall be entitled to be paid for all of the Sub Contract Works properly executed but shall be entitled to no further payment and the Sub-Contractor shall not be entitled to claim loss of profit, loss of expectation or any other loss caused by or arising from such termination.

children.name: text
children: Following the termination of this Agreement:

children.name: text
children: the Sub-Contractor shall immediately leave the Site and deliver to the Company all drawings, details, documents and information prepared or being prepared by or on behalf of the Sub-Contractor for the Sub Contract Works

children.name: text
children: the Company may at its discretion take possession of or use all temporary buildings, plant, tools, equipment, goods and materials supplied by the Sub-Contractor which are on Site;

children.name: text
children: the Company may pay any supplier or Sub-contractor for any materials or goods delivered or work executed for the purposes of the Contract whether before or after the termination insofar as the price thereof has not already been paid by the Sub-Contractor;

children.name: text
children: the Sub-Contractor shall if so required by the Company assign to the Company without payment the benefit of any agreement for the supply of materials or goods and / or for the execution of any work for the purpose of the carrying out of the Sub Contract Works; and

children.name: text
children: the Sub-Contractor shall as and when required by the written direction of the Company (but not before) remove from the Site any temporary buildings, plant, tools, equipment, goods and materials belonging to or hired by the Sub-Contractor. If within a reasonable time thereafter the Sub-Contractor has not complied with the written instruction then the Company may (but without responsibility for any loss or damage) remove and sell any such property of the Sub-Contractor holding the proceeds less all costs incurred by the Company in respect of any such removal or sale to the credit of the Sub-Contractor’s account.

children.name: text
children: Save for termination of the employment of the Sub-Contractor pursuant to clause 17.3, all damages, direct or indirect costs and expenses incurred by the Company as a result of the determination of the Contract for any reason whatsoever including the employment of alternative Sub-Contractor(s) to carry out and complete the remaining Sub Contract Works shall be set off against any monies due to the Sub-Contractor. For the avoidance of doubt costs and expenses will include but not be limited to all administration and management costs, all finance costs and any other costs and expenses related to any delay in the Company’s receipt of revenue.

children.name: text
children: Save for termination of the employment of the Sub-Contractor pursuant to clause 17.3, if the employment of the Sub-Contractor is terminated for any reason whatsoever, the Company shall not be bound to make any further payment to the Sub-Contractor until the full and final cost of completion of the Sub Contract Works by others has been ascertained. If the amount of any such damage, loss and/or expense exceeds in total the amount due to the Sub-Contractor up to the date of termination, the difference shall be a debt payable to the Company by the Sub-Contractor but otherwise be a debt payable to the Sub-Contractor. The Sub-Contractor shall not be entitled to loss of profit.

children.name: text
children: In the event of cancellation of the Project or any part of the Project for any reason at any time the Company shall be entitled to omit all or any part or parts of the Sub Contract Works from the Contract as a Variation by giving notice in writing to the Sub-Contractor and shall not be liable to the Sub-Contractor for any loss and/or expense or compensation for loss of profit. The value of such a Variation shall be deducted from the Contract Sum.

children.name: text
children: If the Company’s employment under the main contract is terminated / determined the Sub-Contractors employment under this agreement shall automatically be terminated.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor shall be liable for and shall indemnify and keep indemnified the Company against all liabilities which the Company may incur or may be liable for, without limit to include for personal injury, death damage to property (real or personal), other claim or cost, as a result of or in connection with the execution, completion and/or defects rectification of the Sub Contract Works whether on or off Site.

children.name: text
children: All equipment materials and goods not for incorporation into the Sub Contract Works brought on Site shall be at the sole risk of the Sub Contractor.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor warrants that he has not entered and shall not enter into any contracts with suppliers or sub-contractors which contain a retention of title clause and property in materials and goods supplied to the Sub Contractor shall pass unconditionally to the Sub Contractor no later than the date on which they are included in the relevant Interim Payment.

children.name: text
children: The property in any goods and materials intended for the Sub Contract Works shall vest in the Company as and when the Sub Contractor has received payment for the same or the same has been delivered to Site whichever is the earlier.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor shall be responsible for any damage to equipment material and goods properly brought on Site and the Sub Contractor shall be responsible for any damage to them and shall remain liable for their safe keeping until practical completion of the Project.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor shall indemnify the Company from and against any and all losses, expenses, liabilities, claims, costs or proceedings whatsoever arising from any failure by the Sub Contractor to perform fully his obligations under this clause 19 including any failure to pass to the Company a complete and unencumbered title in and to any materials or goods or items which become the property of the Company.

children.name: text
children: If at any time a dispute or difference shall arise between the Company and the Sub Contractor then, within 7 days of either party notifying the other of such dispute of difference, the Managing Directors or other Director nominated by either party, shall attend a meeting to discuss and seek to resolve the relevant dispute or difference.

children.name: text
children: If a dispute or difference arises under this Sub Contract which either Party wishes to refer to adjudication, the Scheme shall apply, subject to the following:

children.name: text
children: for the purposes of the Scheme the Adjudicator shall be the person (if any) and the nominating body shall be that stated in the Sub Contract Particulars;

children.name: text
children: where the dispute or difference is or includes a dispute or difference relating to clause 4.1.1 and as to whether a direction issued thereunder is reasonable in all the circumstances:

children.name: text
children: the Adjudicator to decide such dispute or difference shall (where practicable) be an individual with appropriate expertise and experience in the in the specialist area or discipline relevant to the direction or issue in dispute;

children.name: text
children: if the Adjudicator does not have the appropriate expertise and experience, the Adjudicator shall appoint an independent expert with such expertise and experience to advise and report in writing on whether or not the direction under clause 4.1.1 is reasonable in all the circumstances.

children.name: text
children: the Responding Party to any adjudication shall have a minimum of 14 days from receipt of the Referral Notice to respond to the Referral Notice, and such response shall not be limited in the number of words or documents

children.name: text
children: The Adjudicator shall have jurisdiction to consider and determine any matter raised by the Company in its response to a Referral Notice served by the Sub Contractor, including but not limited to, any counterclaims, set offs or abatements which the Company might raise in its response, notwithstanding the fact that the Company may have failed to serve a notice of intention to withhold payment pursuant to section 111 of the Housing Grants, Construction and Regeneration Act 1996 and/or pursuant to clause 11.6 of the Sub Contract.

children.name: text
children: The Adjudicator’s decision is binding until the dispute or difference is finally determined by the Courts.

children.name: text
children: If requested in writing by the Company the Sub Contractor shall within 7 days at no extra costs provide collateral warranties in the form required under the Main Contract and to the parties indicated in the Sub Contract Particulars.

children.name: text
children: Without prejudice to the Company’s other remedies under these Conditions, if any of the collateral warranties referred to in this clause 21 are not provided to the Company at or within the time specified therein, the Company shall be entitled to deduct or withhold an amount equal to ten per cent (10%) of any payment to which the Sub Contractor would otherwise be entitled under this Sub Contract until such collateral warranty has been provided to the Company. For the avoidance of doubt, the Company shall retain the full legal and beneficial ownership of any monies withheld pursuant to this provision.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor shall not assign its benefit or rights under this Sub Contract.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor may not sublet any part of the Sub Contract Works without the written consent of the Company.

children.name: text
children: The Company shall be entitled to deduct from payments otherwise due to the Sub Contractor the Construction Industry Training Board levy applicable to payments under such agreements. Such deduction shall be at the rate current at the time of the payment unless the Sub Contractor can provide adequate proof that the Sub Contract Works are exempt or the Sub Contractor holds his own CITB registration.

children.name: text
children: The Company may at its discretion from time to time provide plant/ equipment at the site for the non-exclusive use by the Sub Contractor, his workmen and agents. In respect of his use of any such plant/ equipment, the Sub Contractor shall:

children.name: text
children: Whilst the plant/equipment is provided to the sub-contractor, the sub-contractor shalltake full responsibility for the plant whilst under their use. The sub-contractor shallinstruct and supervise the use of the plant, until handed back to the company

children.name: text
children: not remove the plant/equipment from the Site on which the Development is being carried out;

children.name: text
children: ensure that the plant/equipment is kept in good condition, serviceable and clean;

children.name: text
children: allow the Company to terminate the Sub Contractor’s use of the plant/equipment on demand;

children.name: text
children: Indemnify the Company fully against damage or loss of the plant/equipment (including without limitation, accidental damage and theft) caused or contributed to by the Contractor or any person to whom he is responsible;

children.name: text
children: Indemnify the Company fully against damage or loss of which causes an accidental personal injury (including, without limitation, incorrect use, unsupervised use, unauthorised use) caused or contributed to by the Contractor or any person;

children.name: text
children: be liable in relation to any civil responsibility or liability in respect of the Contractor’s use of the plant/equipment and such use is at the Sub Contractor’s own risk and no warranty or other liability on the part of the Company or of its other contractors will be created or implied in regard to the fitness, condition or suitability of such plant/equipment. The conditions of clause 14.5 will apply to damage caused to or arising out of the use of such plant/equipment by the Sub Contractor and those for whom the Contractor is responsible; and

children.name: text
children: comply with all Statutory Requirements applicable to such use.

children.name: text
children: The Company shall have no liability in the event any plant/equipment or any other goods or services provided by him for the Sub Contractor to use as he requires and the Sub Contractor shall make no claim in relation and have no entitlement thereto.

children.name: text
children: Save where this Agreement expressly provides that items are to be provided by the Company, the Sub Contractor shall provide everything necessary for the carrying out of the Sub Contract Works in accordance with this Agreement including all labour, plant, tools, craneage, safety equipment, protection clothing, consumables and materials.

children.name: text
children: The Company may at its discretion from time to time provide materials at the site for the use by the Sub Contractor, his workmen and agents and the provisions of clause 14.5 will apply. There shall be a condition precedent that the Sub Contractor gives the Company 7 days prior notice of its requirement for plant and materials to be on Site or any such other lead periods as may be required by the Company and the lead periods are to be solely at the Company’s discretion.

children.name: text
children: complete the Company’s Health and Safety Questionnaires;

children.name: text
children: co-operate with the Company in fulfilling its health and safety responsibilities;

children.name: text
children: indemnify the Company against loss for any breach by the Sub Contractor of its responsibilities;

children.name: text
children: ensure that H&S documents are prepared in such a way as they may be easily incorporated into the Health and Safety Plan and the Health and Safety File;

children.name: text
children: develop risk assessments, method statements and control of substances hazardous to health (COSHH) assessments;

children.name: text
children: comply with the health and safety requirements of the Site or the Main Contractor including but not limited to the Health and Safety requirements set out in the Working at Height Policy, PPE Policy, Construction Phase Health & Safety Plan and H&S Questionnaire.

children.name: text
children: Provide and maintain PPE required per company or main contractor policies, and anytask-specific PPE required to complete the sub-contract works.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor shall not divulge to any third party or make use of any drawings detailed information prepared on behalf of the Company or the Main Contractor or of any confidential information except for the purposes of the Sub Contract Works and, if so requested by the Company, the Sub Contractor shall return the same to the Company.

children.name: text
children: The Contractor shall not (other than to any person to whom disclosure must be made in order for the Contractor to fulfil his obligations under this Contract or to comply with Statutory Requirements or in relation to information in the public domain) without the Company’s consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed, for any reason disclose to any person, or make use of, any confidential information which he possesses or acquires relating to the Company, any related entity or any beneficiary, their businesses, any project agreements or the Works (including information relating to methods and techniques of construction proposed by the Company, any financial information relating to the Works and the contents of any drawings, details, documents or other information prepared by or on behalf of the Employer) or make any press or other public announcement or divulge or communicate to any person the existence of this Contract.

children.name: text
children: Any notice to be given under this Sub Contract shall be in writing and shall be deemed to be given properly if it is delivered by hand, or sent by registered post or recorded delivery to in the case of the Company its registered office and in the case of the Sub Contractor its registered office/principal place of business or such other address stated in the Sub Contract Particulars.

children.name: text
children: If the notice is sent by registered post or recorded delivery, it shall be deemed to be received two working days after the date it was posted.

children.name: text
children: If the notice is delivered by hand, it shall be deemed to be received on the day it is delivered.

children.name: text
children: In the case of any Payment Notice, Payment Notice in Default and/or Pay Less Notice only, by e-mail, provided always that such notice is given by an e-mail or series of e-mails each one of which is less than 10mb in size where service shall be deemed to have taken place on the day of transmission if sent before 4 pm or on the next business day if sent after 4 pm subject to proof of sending and a further copy of the notice being sent by first class post.

children.name: text
children: Nothing in this Sub Contract shall confer or is intended to confer on any other party any benefit or right against the Company or the Sub Contractor.

children.name: text
children: The laws of England and Wales shall apply to this Sub Contract.

children.name: text
children: Any dispute or difference under this Sub Contract shall be determined by legal proceedings and the English courts shall have jurisdiction over any dispute or difference under or in connection with the Sub Contract or its performance.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor shall and shall procure that any of its officers, employees, agents, advisers, suppliers, service providers or other persons associated with it shall;

children.name: text
children: Comply with all applicable laws, statutes and regulations relating to anti-bribery and anti-corruption including but not limited to the Bribery Act 2010.

children.name: text
children: Comply with the Coinford Anti-Bribery Policy and any subsequent updates.

children.name: text
children: Have and maintain in place throughout the duration of the Agreement your own policies and procedures including (not limited to) adequate procedures under the Bribery Act to ensure compliance, and enforce them where appropriate.

children.name: text
children: Not do or omit to do any act that will cause or lead the Company to be in breach of any relevant laws or the Policy.

children.name: text
children: Promptly report to The Company (in writing) any breach of the relevant laws or the Policy.

children.name: text
children: The Supplier represents that it applies and undertakes that it will continue to apply the supply chain due diligence principles as recommended by HMRC advice and guidelines from time to time and agrees to provide on demand such evidence of its compliance with this clause as the Client may reasonably request.

children.name: text
children: The Supplier agrees to indemnify the Client against any loss, costs, damages, or expenses of the Supplier arising as a result of or in connection with the Supplier’s failure to comply with Clause 9.1 or any intermediary or subcontractor’s failure to comply with the requirements of this Clause 9 pursuant to Clause 9.4.

children.name: text
children: On the Client’s request, the Supplier will provide all information necessary to enable the Client to carry out supply chain due diligence in accordance with HMRC advice and guidelines from time to time and following good industry practice. Such information shall include (without limitation) the timely completion of Client questionnaires and providing evidence of tax compliance such as screen shots of HMRC tax portals, CIS returns, VAT returns, payslips and any other tax related documents. A questionnaire is at Schedule 5 and will be required to be completed at least annually.

children.name: text
children: The Supplier agrees that it shall not use intermediaries or subcontractors to deliver the Construction Services or perform any of its obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the Client. If the Client agrees to such use of an intermediary or subcontractor, then (subject always to Clause 16.2) the Supplier undertakes to procure that such intermediary or subcontractor complies with the obligations on the Supplier under this Clause 9 as if such intermediary was the Supplier.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor shall be responsible for ensuring the personnel has the legal right to work in the UK and is required to retain copies of recognised right to work documentation. The Sub Contractor agrees to provide copies of this right to work documentation to the Company if requested to do so. The Sub Contractor further undertakes to indemnify and hold the Company harmless if the Sub Contractor has engaged personnel who do not have the right to work in the UK.

children.name: text
children: In performing its obligations under this Contract, the Sub Contractor shall and (if applicable) shall ensure that each of its subcontractors shall comply with the Modern Slavery Act 2015.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor represents and warrants that:

children.name: text
children: it conducts its business in a manner that is consistent with the Modern Slavery Act 2015;

children.name: text
children: neither the Supplier nor any of its officers, employees or other persons associated with it:

children.name: text
children: has been convicted of any offence involving slavery and human trafficking; and

children.name: text
children: has been or is the subject of any investigation, inquiry or enforcement proceedings by any governmental, administrative or regulatory body regarding any offence or alleged offence of or in connection with slavery and human trafficking.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor shall implement due diligence procedures for its own suppliers, subcontractors and other participants in its supply chains, to ensure that there is no slavery or human trafficking in its supply chains.

children.name: text
children: If Coinford permits the Sub Contractor to subcontract its obligations, the Sub Contractor shall implement an appropriate system of due diligence, audit and training designed to ensure compliance with the Modern Slavery Act 2015.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor shall notify the Company as soon as it becomes aware of:

children.name: text
children: any breach, or potential breach, of the Modern Slavery Act 2015; or

children.name: text
children: any actual or suspected slavery or human trafficking in a supply chain which has a connection with this Contract.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor shall prepare and deliver to the Company no later than 1st May in each year or at such other time on request by the Company, an annual slavery and human trafficking report setting out the steps it has taken to ensure that slavery and human trafficking is not taking place in any of its supply chains or in any part of its business.

children.name: text
children: maintain a complete set of records to trace the supply chain of all Goods and/or Services provided to the Company in connection with this Contract; and

children.name: text
children: implement annual supplier and subcontractor audits, either directly or through a third party auditor to monitor compliance with the Modern Slavery Act 2015.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor shall implement a system of training for its employees to ensure compliance with the Modern Slavery Act 2015.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor shall keep a record of all training offered and completed by its employees to ensure compliance with the Modern Slavery Act 2015 and shall make a copy of the record available to the Company on request.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor shall indemnify the Company against any losses, liabilities, damages, costs (including but not limited to legal fees) and expenses incurred by, or awarded against, the Company as a result of any breach of the Modern Slavery Act 2015.

children.name: text
children: The Employer / Company for the contract described will be Coinford Ltd.

children.name: text
children: The site of the works described is as set out in the invitation to tender or the letter of appointment.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contract Works will consist of those works as described in:

children.name: text
children: the invitation to tender and the letter of appointment if no Sub Contract Agreement has been executed OR

children.name: text
children: the Contract Documents and Sub Contract Agreement executed (“the Sub Contract Works”).

children.name: text
children: All Sub Contract Works will be carried out in accordance with and subject to the terms and conditions set out in:

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contract Agreement which includes the Sub Contract Particulars which include theContract Documents; and

children.name: text
children: The Coinford Limited Sub Contract Terms and Conditions (pages 1 to 38 inclusive) andapplicable trade specifications set out in this documents and;

children.name: text
children: The Safety Management Rules and Requirements for Contractors and Sub-Contractors.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor shall make due allowance for compliance with these Conditions.

children.name: text
children: A copy of all documents is available for inspection at the Company’s offices noted above.

children.name: text
children: No undertaking is given that the tender selected for contract will be the lowest tender price submitted.

children.name: text
children: The terms 'approved', 'directed' or ’selected' means the approval, direction or selection by the Company or its appointed consultants. Where the word 'allow' occurs in this specification the cost of the item shall be entirely at the risk of the Sub Contractor employed.

children.name: text
children: The drawings to which these conditions apply are those scheduled, agreed and included as Contract Documents in the Sub Contract Agreement, or if no Sub Contract Agreement is executed, as included in the Letter of Enquiry and Letter of Appointment/Order. The Sub Contractor shall satisfy himself fully as to the accuracy and sufficiency of the drawings provided and the extent of the work involved. The Sub Contractor shall immediately advise the Company of any discrepancies, errors or omissions prior to commencement of the Sub Contract Works. No payment for extra works will be made due to failure on behalf of the Sub Contractor to acquaint himself fully with the extent of the works or due to the failure to identify discrepancies etc. If the Sub Contractor is carrying out Sub Contract Works which include design, then the Contractor shall be fully responsible in all respects for the design of the Sub Contract Works and shall adopt and take responsibility for any design work in relation thereto including any design produced by the Company/ Employer/ or their Agent, which design is included in the Contractor’s Proposals. Without prejudice to the generality thereof, the Sub Contractor shall be fully responsible and liable to the Employer/Company for the selection of goods and materials, workmanship and the satisfaction of performance specifications.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor is to be responsible for complying with all current legislation in respect of Income Tax, National Insurance contributions, pension scheme, holiday with pay and death benefit schemes and is deemed to have included for all his liabilities under same.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor shall comply with all appropriate conditions of the National Joint Council for the Building Industry and shall maintain appropriate proper records on wages, holidays with pay etc. The Company reserves the right to close the site during any holiday period declared by the NJ Council and during the Christmas period as appropriate.

children.name: text
children: The whole of the Sub Contract Works shall be constructed to the highest achievable standard and to the complete satisfaction of the Company, appointed consultants, NHBC, Local Authority or Statutory Authority applicable. Any such work rejected on the grounds of inferior workmanship or materials or non-compliance shall be made good at the Contractor’s expense and he shall be responsible for all direct and indirect costs or consequential losses incurred by the Company.

children.name: text
children: Throughout these General Conditions and any Contract Documents unless otherwise stated, all materials are to comply with the latest relevant British Standard Specification, NHBC, Local Authority and NIECC requirements and ECC conditions.

children.name: text
children: Where and to the extent that materials, products and workmanship are not fully detailed or specified they are to be:

children.name: text
children: - Of a standard appropriate to the Sub Contract Works and suitable for the functions in or reasonably to be inferred from the Contract Documents.

children.name: text
children: - In accordance with good building practice.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor shall submit to the Company a written certification from the product manufacturer / supplier that the materials / components / systems specified have been reviewed and approved by them, as completely appropriate / 'fit for purpose' for their intended use in the Sub Contract Works, with regard to all functions, design and construction criteria plus all other requirements of the Contract Documents, and are compatible with all components and adjacent materials, together with life expectancy of the materials detailed and specified.

children.name: text
children: Products to be new unless otherwise specified.

children.name: text
children: For products specified to a British or European Standard, the Sub Contractor shall obtain certificates of compliance from manufacturers when requested by the Company.

children.name: text
children: Where a choice of manufacturer or source of supply is allowed for any particular product, the whole quantity required to complete the work must be of the same type, manufacturer and/or source unless otherwise approved.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor shall produce written evidence of sources of supply when requested by the Company.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor shall ensure that the whole quantity of each product required to complete the work is of consistent kind, size, quality and overall appearance.

children.name: text
children: Where consistency of appearance is desirable the Sub Contractor shall ensure consistency of supply from the same source. Unless otherwise approved do not use different colour batches where they can be seen together.

children.name: text
children: If products are prone to deterioration or have a limited shelf life, the Sub Contractor shall order the products in suitable quantities to a programme and use in appropriate sequence. Do not use if there are any signs of deterioration, settling or other unsatisfactory condition.

children.name: text
children: Handle, store, prepare and use or fix each product in accordance with its manufacturers' current printed or written recommendations / instructions. Inform the Company if these conflicts with any other specified requirement. Submit copies to the Company when requested.

children.name: text
children: The tender will be deemed to be based on the products specified and recommendations on their use as described in the manufacturers' literature.

children.name: text
children: Where British Board of Agreement certified products are used, comply with the limitations, recommendations and requirements of the relevant valid certificates.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor shall check all delivery tickets, labels, identification marks, and where appropriate, the products themselves to ensure that all products comply with the project documents. Where different types of any product are specified, check to ensure that the correct type is being used in each location.

children.name: text
children: In particular the Sub Contractor shall check that:

children.name: text
children: - The sources, types, qualities, finishes and colours are correct, and match any approved samples.

children.name: text
children: - All accessories and fixings which should be supplied with the goods have been supplied.

children.name: text
children: - Sizes and dimensions are correct. Where tolerances of components are critical, measure a sufficient quantity to ensure compliance.

children.name: text
children: - The delivered quantities are correct, to ensure that shortages do not cause delays in the work.

children.name: text
children: - The products are clean, undamaged and otherwise in good condition.

children.name: text
children: - Products which have a limited shelf life are not out of date.

children.name: text
children: Prevent over stressing, distortion and any other type of physical damage.

children.name: text
children: Keep clean and free from contamination.

children.name: text
children: Prevent staining, chipping, scratching or other disfigurement, particularly of products exposed to view in the finished work.

children.name: text
children: Keep dry and in a suitably low humidity atmosphere to prevent premature setting, moisture movement and similar defects. Where appropriate store off the ground and allow free air movement around and between stored products.

children.name: text
children: Prevent excessively high or low temperatures and rapid changes of temperature in the products.

children.name: text
children: Protect adequately from rain, damp, frost, sun and other elements as appropriate.

children.name: text
children: Ensure that products are at a suitable temperature and moisture content at time of use.
Ensure that sheds and covers are of ample size, in good weatherproof condition and well secured.

children.name: text
children: Keep different types of grades of products separately and adequately identified.

children.name: text
children: So far as possible keep products in their original wrapping, packing or containers, until immediately before they are used.

children.name: text
children: Wherever possible retain protective wrappings after fixing and shortly before Practical Completion.

children.name: text
children: Ensure that protective measures are fully compatible with and not prejudicial to the products / materials.

children.name: text
children: SUITABILITY OF RELATED WORK AND CONDITIONS

children.name: text
children: - Ensure that all trades are provided with necessary details of related types of work.

children.name: text
children: Before starting each new type or section of work ensure that:

children.name: text
children: - Previous, related work is appropriately complete, in accordance with the project documents, to a suitable standard and in a suitable condition to receive the new work.

children.name: text
children: - All necessary preparatory work has been carried out, including provision for services, openings, supports, fixings, damp proofing, priming and sealing.

children.name: text
children: - The environmental conditions are suitable, particularly that the building is suitably weather tight when internal components, services and finishes are installed.

children.name: text
children: Operatives must be appropriately skilled and experienced for the type and quality of work.

children.name: text
children: Take all necessary precautions to prevent damage to the work from frost, rain and other hazards.

children.name: text
children: Inspect components and products carefully before fixing or using and reject any which are defective.

children.name: text
children: Fix or lay securely, accurately and in alignment.

children.name: text
children: Where not specified otherwise, select fixing and jointing methods and types, sizes and spacing of fastenings in compliance with manufacturers recommendations. Fastenings to comply with relevant British Standards.

children.name: text
children: Provide suitable, tight packings at screwed and bolted fixing points to take up tolerances and prevent distortion. Do not over tighten fixings.

children.name: text
children: Adjust location and fixing of components and products so that joints which are to be finished with mortar or sealant or otherwise left open to view are even and regular.

children.name: text
children: Ensure that all moving parts operate properly and freely.

children.name: text
children: Do not cut, grind or plane pre-finished components and products to remedy binding or poor fit without approval.

children.name: text
children: Where compliance with BS 8000 is specified, this is only to the extent that the recommendations therein define the quality of the finished work.

children.name: text
children: Where BS 8000 gives recommendations on particular working methods or other matters which are properly in the province and responsibility of the Contractor, compliance therewith will be deemed to be a matter of general industry good practice and not a specific requirement of the Company under the Contract.

children.name: text
children: If there is any conflict or discrepancy between the recommendations of BS 8000 on the one hand and the Contract Documents on the other, the Contract Documents will prevail.

children.name: text
children: WATER FOR THE SUB CONTRACT WORKS

children.name: text
children: Clean and uncontaminated. If other than mains supply is proposed provide evidence of suitability. Test to BS 3148 if instructed.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor is deemed to have visited and inspected the site and fully satisfied himselfwith all local conditions and difficulties thereof, means of access/egress, feasibility ofunloading, storage of materials, housekeeping of works area, underfoot conditions and allother aspects of the works. If any concerns are identified during the inspection then thesemust be raised in writing to the Company.

children.name: text
children: The Company shall not be liable for any losses however incurred by the Sub Contractor arising out of insufficient or inaccurate information given.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor shall make all necessary enquiries with the Local Authorities or Statutory Authorities to familiarise himself with the location of all existing services and drainage and any damage or cost incurred due to lack of such knowledge must be borne by the Contractor.

children.name: text
children: Any works carried out to or which affects new or existing services must be in accordance with the Bye Laws or Regulations of the relevant Statutory Authority.

children.name: text
children: The Employer makes no guarantee of the programme on the development and reserves the right to phase the works and amend the programme to suit the Company’s requirements and no claims for loss and expense or otherwise arising out of the foregoing will be entertained. Allowance should be made for any out of sequence work should the need arise.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor shall satisfy himself as to the acceptability of all surfaces or bases so prepared to receive his works and shall notify the Company in writing of any areas where he is not satisfied. Should any area of work fail due to the background being unsuitable and no notification prior to commencing the work as such has been received, then the Sub Contractor shall be liable to make good any such defective works at his own expense.

children.name: text
children: Where approval of a product is specified the requirement for approval relates to a sample of the product and not to the product as used in the Sub Contract Works.
Submit a sample or other evidence of suitability.
Do not confirm orders or use the product until approval of the sample has been obtained.
Retain approved sample in good, clean condition on site. Ensure that the product used in the Sub Contract Works matches the approved sample.

children.name: text
children: Where a sample of finished work is specified for approval, the requirement for approval relates to the sample itself (if approval of the finished work as a whole is required this is specified separately).
Obtain approval of the stated characteristic(s) of the sample before proceeding with the Sub Contract Works. Retain approved sample in good, clean condition on site.
Ensure that the relevant characteristic(s) of the Sub Contract Works match the approved characteristic(s) of the sample.
Remove samples which are not part of the finished Sub Contract Works when no longer required.

children.name: text
children: Where and to the extent that products are specified to be approved or the Company instructs or requires that they are to be approved, the same must be supplied and executed to comply with all other requirements and in respect of the stated or implied characteristics either:
- To the express approval of the Company.
- To match a sample expressly approved by the Company as a standard for the purpose.
Inspection or any other action by the Company must not be taken as approval of products or work unless the Company so confirms in writing in express terms referring to:
- Respects or characteristics which are approved
- Extent and purpose of the approval

Any such approval by the Company shall in no way relieve the Sub Contractor of its responsibility to ensure that all materials and products comply with the Sub Contract Agreement and are fit for purpose and of good quality.

children.name: text
children: Use instruments and methods described in BS 5606.

children.name: text
children: Submit details of methods and equipment to be used in setting out the Sub Contract Works.

Check the levels and dimensions of the site against those shown on the drawings, and record the results on a copy of the drawings. Notify the Company in writing of any discrepancies and obtain instructions before proceeding.

Inform the Company when setting out is complete and before commencing construction and also notify the Company in writing of any discrepancies and obtain instructions before proceeding / construction.

children.name: text
children: Arrange the setting out, erection, juxtaposition of components and application of finishes (working within the practical limits of the design and the specification) to ensure that there is satisfactory fit at junctions, that there are no practically or visually unacceptable changes in plane, line or level and that the finished work has a true and regular appearance.

Wherever satisfactory accuracy, fit and/or appearance of the work are likely to be critical or difficult go achieve, obtain approval of proposals or of the appearance of the relevant aspects of the partially finished works as early as possible.
Without prejudice to the above and unless specified otherwise, tolerances will (where applicable) be not greater than those given in BS 5606, Tables 1 and 2.

children.name: text
children: Certain dimensions on the drawings are critical; set out and construct the works to ensure compliance with the tolerances stated on the drawings.

children.name: text
children: Maximum tolerances for designed levels to be as follows:

children.name: text
children: - Floors which are to be self-finished, and floors to receive sheet or tile finishes directly bedded in adhesive: +/- 5mm

children.name: text
children: - Floors to receive dry board / panel construction with little or no tolerance on thickness: +/- 5mm

children.name: text
children: - Floors to receive mastic asphalt flooring / underlays directly: +/- 10mm

children.name: text
children: - Floors to receive mastic asphalt flooring / underlays laid on mastic asphalt levelling coat(s): +/- 10mm

children.name: text
children: - Floors to receive fully bonded screeds / toppings / beds: +/- 10mm

children.name: text
children: - Floors to receive un-bonded or floating screeds / beds: +/- 15mm

children.name: text
children: (Where contract specific tolerances have been stated elsewhere, they will take precedence over the above general requirements.)

children.name: text
children: Record details of all grid lines, setting out stations, bench marks and profiles on the site setting-out drawing. Retain on site throughout the contract and hand to the Company on completion.

children.name: text
children: The subcontractor shall comply with the Company’s Permit to Break Ground procedure whenever any works require breaking the ground. This will include obtaining a Permit to Break ground, using buried services detection equipment, and utilising safe digging practices as covered in HSG47.
Make adequate provision for services, including unobstructed routes and fixings. Wherever possible ducts, chases and holes are to be formed during construction rather that cut.

children.name: text
children: Must have final tests and commissioning carried out so that they are in full working order at Practical Completion.

children.name: text
children: In addition to the constant management and supervision of the Sub Contract Works provided by the Sub Contractor’s person in charge, all significant types of work must be under the close control of competent trade supervisors to ensure maintenance of satisfactory quality and progress.

children.name: text
children: The site organisation staff must include one or more persons with appropriate knowledge and experience of mechanical and electrical engineering services to ensure compatibility between engineering services, one with another and each in relation to the Sub Contract Works generally. Submit to the Company, when requested, CV’s or other documentary evidence relating to staff concerned.

children.name: text
children: Give maximum possible notice to the Company before changing the person-in-charge.

children.name: text
children: Whenever overtime is to be worked, give the Company not less than 3 days notice, specifying times, types and locations of work to be done.
Concealed work executed during overtime for which notice has not been given may be required to be opened up for inspection and reinstated at the Contractor’s expense.

children.name: text
children: Give the Company not less than 5 days notice before removing scaffolding or other facilities for access.

children.name: text
children: Agree dates and times of tests and inspections with the Company several days in advance, to enable the Company and other affected parties to be present. On the previous working day to each such test or inspection confirm that the work or sample in question will be ready or, if not ready, agree a new date and time.

children.name: text
children: Submit a copy of each certificate to the Company as soon as practicable and keep copies of all certificates on site.

children.name: text
children: PROPOSALS FOR RECTIFICATION OF DEFECTIVE WORK / PRODUCTS

As soon as possible after any part(s) of the work or any products are known to be not in accordance with the Contract or appear that they may not be in accordance submit proposals to the Company for opening up, inspection, testing, making good, adjustment of the Contract Sum, or removal and re-execution.

children.name: text
children: Such proposals may be unacceptable to the Company who may issue contrary instructions.

children.name: text
children: Wherever inspection or testing shows that the work, materials or goods are not in accordance with the Contract and measures (e.g. testing, opening up, experimental making good) are taken to help in establishing whether or not the work is acceptable, such measures:
- will be at the expense of the Sub Contractor
- will not be considered as grounds for extension of time

children.name: text
children: - Establish and maintain procedures to ensure that the Sub Contract Works, including the work of all subcontractors, comply with specified requirements.
- Maintain full records, keep copies on site for inspection by the Company, and submit copies of particular parts of the records on request.

children.name: text
children: - Identification of the element, item, batch or lot including location in the Sub Contract Works
- the nature and dates of inspections by the Sub Contractor or the Company, tests and approvals
- the nature and extent of any non-conforming work found
No payment will be made for any work that is not certified as 100% complete and to the required standards.

children.name: text
children: - Make good all damage consequent upon the work.
- Remove all temporary markings, coverings and protective wrappings unless otherwise instructed.

- Clean the works thoroughly inside and out including all accessible ducts and voids, remove all splashes, deposits, efflorescence, rubbish and surplus materials consequent upon the execution of the work.
- Cleaning materials and methods to be as recommended by manufacturers of products being cleaned, and to be such that there is no damage or disfigurement to other materials or construction.
- Obtain COSHH dated data sheets for all materials used for cleaning and ensure they are used only as recommended by their manufacturers.
- Touch up minor faults in newly painted / repainted work, carefully matching colour, and brushing out edges. Repaint badly marked areas back to suitable breaks or junctions.
- Adjust, ease and lubricate moving parts of new work as necessary to ensure easy and efficient operation, including doors, windows, drawers, ironmongery, appliances, valves and controls.

children.name: text
children: Leave the works secure with all accesses locked. Account for and adequately label all keys and hand over to the Company with itemised schedule, retaining duplicate schedule signed by the Company as receipt.

children.name: text
children: Make arrangements with the Company to give reasonable notice of the precise dates for access to the various parts of the Sub Contract Works for purpose of making good defects. Inform the Company when remedial works to the various parts of the Sub Contract Works are completed.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor warrants and undertakes that the Contract Sum represents all that which is necessary for the carrying out of his obligations under or in connection with this Contract and such sum shall only be increased in respect of the occurrence of any matter which the Conditions expressly provide for an increase in the Contract Sum and shall be subject to the Sub Contractor having complied with the terms of such Conditions.

children.name: text
children: All contractors are required to maintain the workplace in a clean and tidy condition, both during and after any respective operation. Should a contractor fail to keep the workplace clean and tidy, then the Company reserve the right to have the workplace cleaned and/or tidied at the expense of the failing contractor.

children.name: text
children: The Company insists that all defects reported by customers within the defects liability period are to be attended to promptly, efficiently and above all courteously, with key trades on a 24hr call basis and non key trades on a 72hr call out. The Contractors' supervisors will be responsible for co-ordinating the required remedial works and will confirm to the Company when the works have been completed satisfactorily. Should the offending contractor fail to rectify any defective works, the Company reserve the right to employ alternative contractors to complete the remedial works on behalf of the offending contractor.

children.name: text
children: All sub-contractor operatives must attend a Company (and client if applicable) site induction before commencing works on site. A Site induction form must be completed and signed by every subcontractor operative. Copies of training records must be provided at this time. Refusal to complete an induction or provide appropriate training records will prevent operatives from commencing on-site.

children.name: text
children: The subcontractor must provide siter- and task-specific Risk assessment and method statements for the work they are completing before starting on site. All new operatives inducted onto site must be briefed on the RAMS and sign to say they understand the RAMS and will adhere to the safe system of work at all time. Works must not differ from the agreed methodology outlined within the RAMS. Any change to the RAMS must be approved by the company's site management team.

children.name: text
children: These Terms and Conditions apply to all training and development activities within the subcontractor.

children.name: text
children: Sub-contractor is committed to enhancing the skills and knowledge of its employees to ensure high standards of construction safety and efficiency. All site operatives will hold the appropriate CSCS card for the role they are completing. All managers and supervisors will hold appropriate SMSTS/SSSTS training. All plant operators will hold CPCS/NPORS plant training for the category of plant being operated.

children.name: text
children: Attendance is mandatory for all training sessions the Company deems suitable and improves H&S. The cost of such training could be deducted from the sub-contractor.All training costs incurred by the subcontractor will be covered by the subcontractor, including materials and any travel expenses if applicable.

children.name: text
children: The subcontractor will maintain records of training completion, and copies of certificates must be provided during site induction.

children.name: text
children: Non-compliance with these T&Cs may result in disciplinary action, including potential contract termination.

children.name: text
children: Employees must apply skills and knowledge learned during training to their daily tasks.

children.name: text
children: Under no circumstances shall the Sub Contractor alter or interfere with scaffold structures oredge protection systems erected for access and working platforms.

children.name: text
children: Contractors must satisfy themselves that scaffold access and working platforms are in good condition and suitable for themselves and their employees' use. Defects notes or alterations required must be notified to the Company to allow a qualified scaffolder to carry out any necessary works.

children.name: text
children: Contractors must ensure that they or their employees do not overload scaffolds/platformswith materials creating the danger of collapse. Quantities of materials on the scaffold must bekept to the minimum required to keep the work progressing.

children.name: text
children: Materials must be stacked neatly close to the standards and kept well below guardrail height.

children.name: text
children: Scaffold platforms must be kept free of waste materials and at least two boards wide kept clear for access.

children.name: text
children: Throwing or dropping materials down to ground level from any scaffold will not be tolerated and offending Contractors' employees will be removed from the project.

children.name: text
children: All contractors' plant and equipment (owned or hired) is to be thoroughly inspected before being put to work on site. Weekly inspections are to be recorded on site and all relevant test certificates to be made available on site.

children.name: text
children: All electrical portable tools will be restricted to 110v and requires PAT certificates unless written approval is obtained from the Safety Officer.

children.name: text
children: It is a requirement of the Contract that all personnel wear the appropriate PPE to satisfaction of site manager at all times when on site or as directed by the Site Manager.

children.name: text
children: The Subcontractor will always accept the authority of the Safety Officer, Safety Consultant,and Site Manager regarding all Health and safety matters.

children.name: text
children: A serious breach of the Project Health & Safety Policy could lead to termination of the Contract and any costs as a result may be withheld from any monies due.

children.name: text
children: A Sub Contractor employing 20 or more persons must appoint an experienced and qualified Safety Officer.

children.name: text
children: A Sub Contractor employing 5 or more persons must appoint an experienced and qualified First Aider.

children.name: text
children: The requirements of Health & Safety at Work Act 1974 and all future / subsequent Codes of Practice or Regulations issued under the Act affecting the Sub Contractor’s activities will be complied with.

children.name: text
children: All accidents must be reported immediately to the Company site management team andrecorded in the Site Accident Book. Specified injury Accidents and Dangerous Occurrences asdefined in the Reporting of Injuries, Disease and Dangerous Occurrence Regulations 2013 mustbe notified to the Site Manager immediately, who in turn must notify the Safety Officer of boththe Company and sub-contractor.

children.name: text
children: Any accident or incident involving injury or damage to a third party must also be immediately notified to the Site Manager. Notification to the Site Manager in pursuance of the above does not release the Contractor from his statutory duties under the Regulations.

children.name: text
children: All new operatives to the Project will receive a mandatory induction at no cost to the Contractor or the Company. The Company also reserves to right to re-induct any operative should it be deemed necessary.

children.name: text
children: All works on site are to be carried out in accordance with the Control of Substances Hazardousto Health (COSHH) Regulations 2002 and the Site Manager is to be informed prior tocommencement on site of any hazardous materials that the Sub Contractor is likely to use inthe course of the Sub Contract Works.

children.name: text
children: Under the Control of Noise at Work Regulations 2005, the Sub Contractor must ensure thatnoise created by their work activities is kept to the lowest level reasonably practicable toprevent damage to hearing.

children.name: text
children: Contractors must ensure that all plant and equipment is adequately silenced or muffled and, where necessary, provide suitable ear protection to employees.

children.name: text
children: Due regard must also be given to permissible times for noisy work operations and other restrictions which may be imposed by Local Authority Environmental Health Officers.

children.name: text
children: Coinford maintain a zero tolerance with regard to the use of Drugs and Alcohol on site or while working, whilst under the influence. The company completes random D&A testing and the subcontractor will be expected to conduct tests when required. Any refusal to complete a D&A will result in termination from the site. The subcontractor will also be required to comply with any client specific requirements for D&A testing. The subcontractor will cover the costs of any D&A testing undertaken by the company.

children.name: text
children: In the event of an Improvement / Prohibition Notice being served on the Employer by a Health & Safety Officer, the Sub Contractor will be notified immediately and the Contractor will comply with the terms of such a notice.

children.name: text
children: The Sub Contractor’s Tender submitted in response to the Company’s invitation to tender/letter of enquiry constitutes an offer subject to the terms and conditions set out or referred to in the invitation to tender/enquiry. The Company’s letter of appointment/Order will also constitute an offer to carry out and complete the works on the terms and conditions set out in the documents listed in that letter of appointment/Order. The Sub Contractor will accept that offer by either executing the Sub Contract Agreement or commencing the works, whichever is the earlier. No terms set out in the Contractor’s tender will be contractual or binding, unless the document setting out those terms and conditions are incorporated into the Sub Contract Agreement by listing that document as Contract Document.
